content.sanskrit:
arcye viṣṇau śilā-dhīr guruṣu nara-matir vaiṣṇave jāti-buddhir
viṣṇor vā vaiṣṇavānāṁ kali-mala-mathane pāda-tīrthe 'mbu-buddhiḥ
śrī-viṣṇor nāmni mantre sakala-kaluṣa-he śabda-sāmānya-buddhir
viṣṇau sarveśvareśe tad-itara-sama-dhīr yasya vā nārakī saḥ
content.translation: One who thinks the Deity in the temple to be made of wood or stone, who thinks of the spiritual master in the disciplic succession as an ordinary man, who thinks the Vaiṣṇava in the Acyuta-gotra to belong to a certain caste or creed or who thinks of caraṇāmṛta or Ganges water as ordinary water is taken to be a resident of hell. (Padma Purāṇa)
content.wbw: arcye — in the Deity; viṣṇau — Lord Viṣṇu; śilā-dhīr — the conception of it as stone; guruṣu — in the spiritual masters; nara-matir — the conception of them as ordinary men; vaiṣṇave — in a Vaiṣṇava; jāti-buddhir — the conception of him as belonging to a caste or creed; viṣṇor — of Viṣṇu; vā — or; vaiṣṇavānāṁ — of the Vaiṣṇavas; kali-mala-mathane — in that which destroys the contamination of Kali; pāda-tīrthe — in the water that has washed the feet, caraṇāmṛta; 'mbu-buddhiḥ — the conception of it as ordinary water; śrī-viṣṇor — of Śrī Viṣṇu; nāmni — in the holy name; mantre — in the mantra; sakala-kaluṣa-he — which destroys all contamination; śabda-sāmānya-buddhir — the conception of it as an ordinary sound; viṣṇau — in Lord Viṣṇu; sarveśvareśe — the Lord of all lords; tad-itara-sama-dhīr — whose conception is that He is equal to anything else; yasya — of whom; vā — or; nārakī — a resident of hell; saḥ — he is.

content.sanskrit:
vande 'haṁ śrī-guroḥ śrī-yuta-pada-kamalaṁ śrī-gurūn vaiṣṇavāṁś ca
śrī-rūpaṁ sāgrajātaṁ saha-gaṇa-raghunāthānvitaṁ taṁ sa-jīvam
sādvaitaṁ sāvadhūtaṁ parijana-sahitaṁ kṛṣṇa-caitanya-devaṁ
śrī-rādhā-kṛṣṇa-pādān saha-gaṇa-lalitā-śrī-viśākhānvitāṁś ca
content.translation: I offer praṇāma unto the lotus feet of my [śikṣā and dīkṣā] gurus, my entire guru-varga, and to all Vaiṣṇavas, to Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī, his elder brother Śrīla Sanātana Gosvāmī, to Śrīla Raghunātha dāsa Gosvāmī, Śrīla Jīva Gosvāmī, and all their associates, to Śrī Advaita Ācārya, the avadhūta Nityānanda Prabhu, Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya Mahāprabhu and all their associates, and to the lotus feet of Śrī Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa, and to Their companions, Śrī Lalitā, Śrī Viśākhā, and all the other sakhīs.
content.wbw: vande — I offer praṇāma to; 'haṁ — I; śrī-guroḥ — of my revered guru; śrī-yuta-pada-kamalaṁ — the beautiful lotus feet; śrī-gurūn — the revered gurus; vaiṣṇavāṁś — the Vaiṣṇavas; ca — and; śrī-rūpaṁ — Śrī Rūpa Gosvāmī; sāgrajātaṁ — together with his elder brother; saha-gaṇa-raghunāthānvitaṁ — accompanied by Raghunātha and their associates; taṁ — him; sa-jīvam — together with Jīva Gosvāmī; sādvaitaṁ — together with Advaita Ācārya; sāvadhūtaṁ — together with the avadhūta Nityānanda Prabhu; parijana-sahitaṁ — accompanied by Their associates; kṛṣṇa-caitanya-devaṁ — Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya Mahāprabhu; śrī-rādhā-kṛṣṇa-pādān — the lotus feet of Śrī Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa; saha-gaṇa-lalitā-śrī-viśākhānvitāṁś — accompanied by Śrī Lalitā, Śrī Viśākhā and all Their companions; ca — and.

content.sanskrit:
oṁ ajñāna-timirāndhasya jñānāñjana-śalākayā
cakṣur unmīlitaṁ yena tasmai śrī-gurave namaḥ
content.translation: I am blinded by the darkness of ignorance, but śrī guru has mercifully opened my eyes, anointing them with the salve of divine knowledge. I offer praṇāma to that śrī gurudeva.
content.wbw: oṁ — sacred syllable oṁ; ajñāna-timirāndhasya — of one blinded by the darkness of ignorance; jñānāñjana-śalākayā — with the salve of divine knowledge; cakṣur — eyes; unmīlitaṁ — opened; yena — by whom; tasmai — to that; śrī-gurave — to śrī gurudeva; namaḥ — praṇāma.

content.sanskrit:
nārāyaṇa-parāyaṇa jadāhaṅkāra-nāśana
rūpānugāmṛta prema prayojanāya te namaḥ
content.translation: O you who are always absorbed in loving service to your spiritual master, Śrīla Bhaktivedānta Nārāyaṇa Gosvāmī! O you whose causeless mercy completely destroys the inert material ego! You are the embodiment of the immortal nectar of pure divine love (prema) in subordination to Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī, which is the highest goal of life (prayojana). I offer my praṇāma unto You, Śrī Prema Prayojana Prabhu.
content.wbw: nārāyaṇa-parāyaṇa — always absorbed in loving service to your spiritual master; jadāhaṅkāra-nāśana — destroyer of the inert material ego; rūpānugāmṛta — immortal nectar in subordination to Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī; prema — pure divine love; prayojanāya — the highest goal of life; te — unto You; namaḥ — obeisances.

subsections.title: Prayers to Śrī Śrīmad Bhaktivedānta Nārāyaṇa Gosvāmī Mahārāja

content.sanskrit:
nama oṁ viṣṇu-pādāya rādhikāyaḥ-priyātmane
śrī-śrīmad-bhaktivedānta-nārāyaṇa iti nāmine
content.translation: I offer praṇāma to oṁ viṣṇupāda Śrī Śrīmad Bhaktivedānta Nārāyaṇa Gosvāmī Mahārāja, who is very dear to Śrīmatī Rādhikā.
content.wbw: nama — praṇāma; oṁ — sacred syllable oṁ; viṣṇu-pādāya — to him who is at the feet of Viṣṇu; rādhikāyaḥ-priyātmane — who is very dear to Śrīmatī Rādhikā; śrī-śrīmad-bhaktivedānta-nārāyaṇa — Śrī Śrīmad Bhaktivedānta Nārāyaṇa; iti — thus; nāmine — to him who is named.

content.sanskrit:
śrī-kṛṣṇa-līlā-kathane su-dakṣam
audārya-mādhurya-guṇaiś ca yuktam
varaṁ vareṇyaṁ puruṣaṁ mahāntaṁ
nārāyaṇaṁ tvāṁ śirasā namāmi
content.translation: O Śrīla Bhaktivedānta Nārāyaṇa Gosvāmī Mahārāja, you are most expert in describing kṛṣṇa-līlā and are fully endowed with the qualities of magnanimity and sweetness. You are the best of all great souls. I bow my head to you.
content.wbw: śrī-kṛṣṇa-līlā-kathane — in describing Śrī Kṛṣṇa’s līlā; su-dakṣam — most expert; audārya-mādhurya-guṇaiś — with the qualities of magnanimity and sweetness; ca — and; yuktam — fully endowed; varaṁ — the best; vareṇyaṁ — most worshipful; puruṣaṁ — person; mahāntaṁ — great; nārāyaṇaṁ — Nārāyaṇa; tvāṁ — you; śirasā — with my head; namāmi — I bow.

content.sanskrit:
tridandīnām bhakta-śiromaṇiṁ ca
śrī-kṛṣṇa-padābja-dhṛtaika-hṛdi
caitanya-līlāmṛta-sāra-sāraṁ
nārāyaṇaṁ tvaṁ satataṁ prapadye
content.translation: Śrīla Nārāyaṇa Gosvāmī, the jewel among tridaṇḍī-sannyāsīs, holds the lotus feet of Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa within his heart and experiences supreme bliss when Kṛṣṇa renders service to Śrīmatī Rādhikā. He is always absorbed in thoughts of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu and the confidential reasons for His divine descent. With deep reverence, I offer my prostrated obeisances at the lotus feet of Śrīla Nārāyaṇa Gosvāmī, who is endowed with innumerable transcendental qualities.
content.wbw: tridandīnām — of the tridaṇḍī-sannyāsīs; bhakta-śiromaṇiṁ — the jewel among devotees; ca — and; śrī-kṛṣṇa-padābja-dhṛtaika-hṛdi — whose one-pointed heart holds the lotus feet of Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa; caitanya-līlāmṛta-sāra-sāraṁ — the essence of the essence of Śrī Caitanya’s nectar-like pastimes; nārāyaṇaṁ — Śrīla Nārāyaṇa Gosvāmī; tvaṁ — to you; satataṁ — always; prapadye — I offer my prostrated obeisances.

subsections.title: Prayers to Śrī Śrīmad Bhaktivedānta Svāmī Mahārāja

content.sanskrit:
nama oṁ viṣṇu-pādāya kṛṣṇa-preṣṭhāya bhūtale
śrīmate bhaktivedānta-svāmin iti nāmine
content.translation: I offer praṇāma to oṁ viṣṇupāda Śrī Śrīmad Bhaktivedānta Svāmī Mahārāja (Śrīla Prabhupāda), who in this world is most dear to Śrī Kṛṣṇa.
content.wbw: nama — praṇāma; oṁ — the sacred syllable oṁ; viṣṇu-pādāya — to Viṣṇupāda; kṛṣṇa-preṣṭhāya — to him who is most dear to Śrī Kṛṣṇa; bhūtale — in this world; śrīmate — to the illustrious; bhaktivedānta-svāmin — Bhaktivedānta Svāmī; iti — thus; nāmine — to him who is named.

content.sanskrit:
namas te sārasvate deve gaura-vāṇī-pracāriṇe
nirviśeṣa-śūnyavādi-pāścātya-deśa-tāriṇe
content.translation: My respectful obeisances unto you, O servant of Sarasvatī Gosvāmī. You preach the message of Śrī Gaurāṅga and thus deliver the Western countries, which are filled with voidism and impersonalism.
content.wbw: namas — respectful obeisances; te — unto you; sārasvate — O servant of Sarasvatī Gosvāmī; deve — O divine one; gaura-vāṇī-pracāriṇe — who preaches the message of Śrī Gaurāṅga; nirviśeṣa-śūnyavādi-pāścātya-deśa-tāriṇe — who delivers the Western countries filled with voidism and impersonalism.

subsections.title: Prayers to Śrī Śrīmad Bhakti Prajñāna Keśava Gosvāmī Mahārāja

content.sanskrit:
nama oṁ viṣṇu-pādāya ācārya-siṁha-rūpiṇe
śrī-śrīmad-bhakti-prajñāna-keśava iti nāmine
content.translation: I offer praṇāma to the lion-like ācārya, oṁ viṣṇupāda Śrī Śrīmad Bhakti Prajñāna Keśava Gosvāmī Mahārāja.
content.wbw: nama — I offer praṇāma; oṁ — the sacred syllable oṁ; viṣṇu-pādāya — to oṁ viṣṇupāda; ācārya-siṁha-rūpiṇe — to the lion-like ācārya; śrī-śrīmad-bhakti-prajñāna-keśava — to Śrī Śrīmad Bhakti Prajñāna Keśava; iti — thus; nāmine — to the one named.

content.sanskrit:
atimartya-caritrāya svāśritānāṁ ca pāline
jīva-duḥkhe sadārttāya śrī-nāma-prema-dāyine
content.translation: His character and activities are transcendental to the modes of nature, and he protects and nurtures those who take shelter of him. He is always aggrieved to see the suffering of the living entities, and he bestows love for śrī nāma.
content.wbw: atimartya-caritrāya — whose character and activities are transcendental to the modes of nature; svāśritānāṁ — of those who take shelter of him; ca — and; pāline — the protector and nurturer; jīva-duḥkhe — at the suffering of the living entities; sadārttāya — always aggrieved; śrī-nāma-prema-dāyine — the giver of love for śrī nāma.

content.sanskrit:
gaurāśraya-vigrahāya kṛṣṇa-kāmaika-cāriṇe
rūpānuga-pravarāya vinodeti-svarūpiṇe
content.translation: He is the shelter of love for Gaurāṅga, and his every action is solely to fulfil the desires of Śrī Kṛṣṇa. He is best among the followers of Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī, and his internal identity is that of Vinoda Mañjarī.
content.wbw: gaurāśraya-vigrahāya — to him who is the shelter of love for Gaurāṅga; kṛṣṇa-kāmaika-cāriṇe — whose every action is solely to fulfil the desires of Śrī Kṛṣṇa; rūpānuga-pravarāya — who is the best among the followers of Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī; vinodeti-svarūpiṇe — whose internal identity is Vinoda Mañjarī.

content.sanskrit:
prabhupādāntaraṅgāya sarva-sad-guṇa-śāline
māyāvada-tamo-ghnāya vedāntārtha-vāde namaḥ
content.translation: He is an intimate associate of Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Prabhupāda, and he is endowed with all auspicious qualities. He eradicates the darkness of māyāvada and reveals the true meaning of Vedānta. I offer praṇāma to him.
content.wbw: prabhupādāntaraṅgāya — to the intimate associate of Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Prabhupāda; sarva-sad-guṇa-śāline — endowed with all auspicious qualities; māyāvada-tamo-ghnāya — to the eradicator of the darkness of māyāvada; vedāntārtha-vāde — to the revealer of the true meaning of Vedānta; namaḥ — obeisances.

subsections.title: Prayers to Śrī Śrīmad Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Gosvāmī Prabhupāda

content.sanskrit:
nama oṁ viṣṇu-pādāya kṛṣṇa-preṣṭhāya bhūtale
śrīmate bhaktisiddhānta-sarasvatīti-nāmine
content.translation: I offer praṇāma to oṁ viṣṇupāda Śrī Śrīmad Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Gosvāmī Ṭhākura Prabhupāda, who, in this world, is most dear to Kṛṣṇa.
content.wbw: nama — obeisances; oṁ — sacred syllable oṁ; viṣṇu-pādāya — to oṁ viṣṇupāda; kṛṣṇa-preṣṭhāya — who is most dear to Kṛṣṇa; bhūtale — in this world; śrīmate — to the glorious; bhaktisiddhānta-sarasvatīti-nāmine — named Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī.

content.sanskrit:
śrī-vārṣabhānavī-devī-dayitāya kṛpābdhaye
kṛṣṇa-sambandha-vijñāna-dāyine prabhave namaḥ
content.translation: I offer praṇāma to Śrī Vārṣabhānavī-dayita dāsa, the manifestation of an ocean of mercy, who grants realization of our eternal relationship with Śrī Kṛṣṇa.
content.wbw: śrī-vārṣabhānavī-devī-dayitāya — to Śrī Vārṣabhānavī-devī-dayita dāsa; kṛpābdhaye — to the manifestation of an ocean of mercy; kṛṣṇa-sambandha-vijñāna-dāyine — who grants realization of our eternal relationship with Śrī Kṛṣṇa; prabhave — to the master; namaḥ — praṇāma.

content.sanskrit:
mādhuryojjvala-premāḍhya-śrī-rūpānuga-bhakti-da
śrī-gaura-karuṇā-śakti-vigrahāya namo 'stu te
content.translation: O Śrīla Sarasvatī Ṭhākura, you deliver śrī rūpānuga-bhakti, which is enriched with ujjvala-mādhurya-prema. You are the embodiment of the mercy potency of Śrī Gaurāṅga. I offer praṇāma unto you.
content.wbw: mādhuryojjvala-premāḍhya-śrī-rūpānuga-bhakti-da — giver of śrī rūpānuga-bhakti, enriched with ujjvala-mādhurya-prema; śrī-gaura-karuṇā-śakti-vigrahāya — to the embodiment of Śrī Gaurāṅga’s mercy potency; namo — obeisances; 'stu — may there be; te — unto you.

content.sanskrit:
namas te gaura-vāṇī-śrī-mūrtaye dīna-tāriṇe
rūpānuga-viruddhāpasiddhānta-dhvānta-hāriṇe
content.translation: I offer obeisances to you, the embodiment of Śrī Gaurāṅga's message. You deliver the fallen and remove the darkness of philosophical misconceptions that are opposed to the precepts taught by Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī.
content.wbw: namas — obeisances; te — to you; gaura-vāṇī-śrī-mūrtaye — embodiment of Śrī Gaurāṅga's message; dīna-tāriṇe — deliverer of the fallen; rūpānuga-viruddhāpasiddhānta-dhvānta-hāriṇe — remover of the darkness of philosophical misconceptions opposed to the precepts taught by Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī.

subsections.title: Prayer to Śrīla Gaura-kiśora dāsa Bābājī Mahārāja

content.sanskrit:
namo gaura-kiśorāya sākṣād-vairāgya-mūrtaye
vipralambha-rasāmbhodhe! pādāmbujāya te namaḥ
content.translation: I offer praṇāma to Śrī Gaura-kiśora dāsa Bābājī Mahārāja, who is the direct embodiment of renunciation. O you who are an ocean of vipralambha-rasa, I offer praṇāma unto your lotus feet.
content.wbw: namo — praṇāma; gaura-kiśorāya — to Śrī Gaura-kiśora; sākṣād-vairāgya-mūrtaye — to the direct embodiment of renunciation; vipralambha-rasāmbhodhe — O ocean of vipralambha-rasa; pādāmbujāya — to the lotus feet; te — your; namaḥ — praṇāma.

content.sanskrit:
namo bhaktivinodāya sac-cid-ānanda-nāmine
gaura-śakti-svarūpāya rūpānuga-varāya te
content.translation: I offer praṇāma to you, Śrīla Saccidānanda Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura, the foremost of rūpānugas and the personal manifestation of Śrī Gaurāṅga's śakti [Gadādhara Paṇḍita].
content.wbw: namo — obeisances, I offer praṇāma; bhaktivinodāya — to Bhaktivinoda; sac-cid-ānanda-nāmine — named Saccidānanda; gaura-śakti-svarūpāya — the personal manifestation of Śrī Gaurāṅga's śakti; rūpānuga-varāya — the foremost of rūpānugas; te — to you.

subsections.title: Prayer to Śrīla Jagannātha dāsa Bābājī Mahārāja

content.sanskrit:
gaurāvirbhāva-bhūmes tvaṁ nirdeṣṭā sajjana-priyaḥ
vaiṣṇava-sārvabhauma śrī-jagannāthāya te namaḥ
content.translation: You indicated the place of Śrī Gaurāṅga's appearance, and you are most dear to the saintly. O Śrīla Jagannātha dāsa Bābājī Mahārāja, leader of the Vaiṣṇavas, I offer praṇāma unto you.
content.wbw: gaurāvirbhāva-bhūmes — the place of Śrī Gaurāṅga's appearance; tvaṁ — you; nirdeṣṭā — indicated; sajjana-priyaḥ — very dear to the saintly; vaiṣṇava-sārvabhauma — O leader of the Vaiṣṇavas; śrī-jagannāthāya — unto Śrīla Jagannātha dāsa Bābājī Mahārāja; te — unto you; namaḥ — praṇāma.

content.sanskrit:
vāñchā-kalpa-tarubhyaś ca kṛpā-sindhubhya eva ca
patitānāṁ pāvanebhyo vaiṣṇavebhyo namo namaḥ
content.translation: I offer praṇāma again and again to the Vaiṣṇavas, who are the saviors of the fallen, who are just like wish-fulfilling desire-trees and who are oceans of mercy.
content.wbw: vāñchā-kalpa-tarubhyaś — to those who are like wish-fulfilling desire-trees; ca — and; kṛpā-sindhubhya — to the oceans of mercy; eva — indeed; ca — and; patitānāṁ — of the fallen; pāvanebhyo — to the saviors; vaiṣṇavebhyo — to the Vaiṣṇavas; namo — obeisances; namaḥ — praṇāma.

content.sanskrit:
namo mahā-vadānyāya kṛṣṇa-prema-pradāya te
kṛṣṇāya kṛṣṇa-caitanya-nāmne gaura-tviṣe namaḥ
content.translation: I offer praṇāma to that greatly munificent Lord who bestows kṛṣṇa-prema. He is Kṛṣṇa Himself, who has assumed a golden complexion and accepted the name Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya.
content.wbw: namo — obeisances; mahā-vadānyāya — to the greatly munificent Lord; kṛṣṇa-prema-pradāya — who bestows kṛṣṇa-prema; te — to You; kṛṣṇāya — to Kṛṣṇa Himself; kṛṣṇa-caitanya-nāmne — who has accepted the name Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya; gaura-tviṣe — who has assumed a golden complexion; namaḥ — obeisances.

content.sanskrit:
he kṛṣṇa karuṇā-sindho dīna-bandho jagat-pate
gopeśa gopikā-kānta rādhā-kānta namo 'stu te
content.translation: O Śrī Kṛṣṇa, You are an ocean of mercy, the friend of the fallen, Lord of the universe, master of the cowherds, beloved of the gopīs, and [above all] the beloved of Śrī Rādhā. I offer praṇāma unto You.
content.wbw: he — O; kṛṣṇa — Śrī Kṛṣṇa; karuṇā-sindho — ocean of mercy; dīna-bandho — friend of the fallen; jagat-pate — Lord of the universe; gopeśa — master of the cowherds; gopikā-kānta — beloved of the gopīs; rādhā-kānta — beloved of Śrī Rādhā; namo — praṇāma; 'stu — may there be; te — unto You.

content.sanskrit:
tapta-kāñcana-gaurāṅgi rādhe vṛndāvaneśvari
vṛṣabhānu-sute devi praṇamāmi hari-priye
content.translation: O Śrī Rādhā, O Gaurāṅgi, whose complexion is like molten gold, You are the queen of Vṛndāvana, the daughter of Vṛṣabhānu, and the divine goddess, who is most dear to Śrī Hari. I offer praṇāma unto You.
content.wbw: tapta-kāñcana-gaurāṅgi — O Gaurāṅgi, whose complexion is like molten gold; rādhe — O Śrī Rādhā; vṛndāvaneśvari — O queen of Vṛndāvana; vṛṣabhānu-sute — O daughter of Vṛṣabhānu; devi — O divine goddess; praṇamāmi — I offer praṇāma unto You; hari-priye — O most dear to Śrī Hari.

subsections.title: Prayer to the Presiding Deity of Sambandha, Śrī Rādhā-Madana-mohana

content.sanskrit:
jayatāṁ su-ratau paṅgor mama manda-mater gatī

content.content: Right after awaking chant ⟦pranama mantra⟧ to Your ⟦Gurudeva⟧.
⟦Śrī Śrī Guru-Gaurāṅga Gāndhārvikā-Giridhārī Rādhā-Vinoda-Bihārījī kī jaya⟧
And chanting the ⟦pañca-tattva-mantra⟧ and the ⟦mahā-mantra⟧. With heartfelt devotion, chant the following prayers:

content.translation: All glories to that Yaśodā-nandana -- around whom a controversy arose because He seemingly took birth from the womb of Devakī, although later, that became uncertain -- who resides within the heart of all. His assembly is decorated with the presence of the exalted Yādavas, and He destroys irreligion with His own might and the help of His devotees. The chanting of His name removes inauspiciousness from all living entities, both moving and stationary. All glories to Vrajendra-nandana Śrī Kṛṣṇa, who's softly smiling lotus face always enhances the transcendental lust of the vraja-gopīs. [Śrī-mad-Bhāgavatam 10.90.48]

content.content: Then one should brush one's teeth, wash face and then bathe after passing stool and put on clean clothes. Pujari do not go to the toilet in clean clothes!

Long nails are dirty and contaminated. Therefore, it is a general practice of pūjārīs to keep their fingernails short, to avoid contaminating the ⟦bhoga⟧ and other articles meant for offering to the Lord. Even during the four months of ⟦Cāturmāsya⟧, pūjārīs keep their nails short. Brush their teeth even on fast days.
Mantra for taking bath by mind (mānasa-snāna)

content.content: After bathing, comb the hair and tie the ⟦śikhā⟧ while remembering the ⟦brahma-gāyatrī⟧, along with the syllable ⟦oṁ⟧.
The ⟦śikhā⟧ is not braided or kept untied and disheveled. It is preferable to tie it with a slip knot.

Do not enter the deity room or the kitchen with contaminated cloth or touch the deity paraphernalia and kitchen pots. Do not clean the deity's paraphernalia or wash the deity's pots while wearing cloth in which one has defecated or slept the night before.
Tīrtha-āvāhana-mantra

Set an empty ⟦pañca-pātra⟧ in place and fill it with fresh water. After pouring a few drops of water from the ⟦ācamana-pātra⟧ or a spouted waterpot onto the fingers of your right hand, purify the ⟦pañca-pātra⟧ by ⟦prokṣaṇa⟧:
Chanting ⟦oṁ astrāya phaṭ⟧, sprinkle water on the ⟦pañca-pātra⟧.
Invoke the ⟦Gaṅgā⟧ and other holy rivers by showing the ⟦aṅkuśamudrā⟧ and chanting:

content.quote: This is the desire. This is the desire of all the Rūpānuga Vaiṣṇavas, only that Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa will meet together. This is why we put tilaka on every day, you see? One side is Rādhikā, one side means Kṛṣṇa. They're parallel lines, so the parallel lines don't meet. But these parallel lines are meeting where, here, this is a tulasī leaf, represents Vṛndā.

more.quote: Our Different lines have different types of tilaka, made of different substances, but our tilaka is gopī-candana. Sometimes there are some devotees from other lines, and they criticize, "Well, what is your tilaka? Why is this Why don't you wear black Rādhā-kuṇḍa tilaka or something?" But you know that Madhvācārya's iṣṭa-deva, Nartaka Gopāla, was found in a ball of gopī-candana. And so all the ācāryas in his line up to our Lakṣmīpati Tīrtha, and Mādhavendra Purī, Īśvara Purī, and Caitanya Mahāprabhu, they received gopī-candana tilaka. Caitanya Mahāprabhu (..) discovered Rādhā-kuṇḍa in his sannyāsa-līlā, in his prakaṭa-līlā. And he took some mud from there and applied it for a few days. But in the aprakaṭa-nitya-līlā of Caitanya Mahāprabhu, he never leaves Navadvīpa, and he always has gopī-candana tilaka. And (..) you can see in the Rādhā-Dāmodara temple that Rūpa Gosvāmī had only one dīkṣā disciple, Jīva Gosvāmī, and they are coming in that line. From Rūpa Gosvāmī, Jīva Gosvāmī, and their tilaka is exactly the same as ours.

source.title: Q&A Meditation in Raganuga Bhakti and When Applying Tilaka - 2024-11-11 - Sri Prem Prayojan

more.quote: The guru gives Tilaka. So now, unlike (..) the branding, we actually do this. And the guru gives tilaka to the disciple. We accept the same tilaka that our guru wears. I know that many devotees, oh Rādhā-kuṇḍa Tilaka, Rādhā-kuṇḍa is so high, let's wear Rādhā-kuṇḍa. Yeah, but my guru wears this tilaka, I wear this tilaka. Rādhā-kuṇḍa may be so high, that's great. But I'll never get to Rādhā-kuṇḍa unless I'm in the ānugatya of my guru. So I wear this, the gopī-candana. In Rāga-vartma-candrikā, Śrīla Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura says that gopī-candana is favorable for Rāgānugā-bhakti. Why? Because it's the dust of the Gopīs' lotus feet. Someone may say, but Caitanya Mahāprabhu wore Rādhā-kuṇḍa tilaka. Yes, in his naimittika-līlā, after he took sannyāsa, he went to Vraja and did parikramā, he discovered Rādhā-kuṇḍa, took some clay and put it on. But actually, we don't worship the sannyāsa form of Caitanya Mahāprabhu. Right? We worship him in his nitya-līlā in Navadvīpa.

source.title: Guru-tattva and Diksha Process - 2025-05-04 - Sri Prem Prayojan

more.quote: So, you know that our tilak is a yellow color. Other sometimes are wearing Rādhā-kuṇḍa tilak, it's gray. Sometimes they say, "Oh, why you wear this tilak from Dvārakā? We don't want to go to Dvārakā." Because our tilak comes from Dvārakā. But actually it's not from Dvārakā, it was imported to Dvārakā from Vṛndāvana. We're just exporting it back. So you can see that our Madhvācārya, he, (..) discovered the lost deity of Narta Gopāla. And how was he? He found Him in a big block of tilak, that means that Kṛṣṇa for 4,000 years was just immersed in gopīs' foot dust.

source.title: Sri Prem Prayojan - 2019-10-18 - Istagosthi 1

more.quote:
So, (..) (..) in the nitya-līlā, Mahāprabhu wears gopī-candana. Why? The gopī-candana is worn by the Mādhvas. It was Mādhvācārya who discovered the Dadhi-manthana Gopāla at the coast just close to Udupi. And where did he discover him? In a big block of gopī-candana.

[…]

So Mādhvācārya came and he touched that block of tilaka and it broke open and inside there was that Dadhi-manthana Gopāla from Dvārakā. So Krishna for more than four thousand years had been completely immersed in the foot dust of Vraja-gopīs. He was feeling, Krishna was feeling separation from Vraja-gopīs there in Dvārakā. And so He completely covered himself for four thousand years in foot dust of Vraja-gopīs to survive. What a bhāva. So Mādhvācārya wears gopī-candana tilaka from Dvārakā.

source.title: 2026.03.17_Istagosthi

more.quote:
Now, what is gopī-candana? Gopī-candana is once Kṛṣṇa was in Dvārakā, and He had a headache. And Nārada came to Him, said, "My Lord, can I do something, how can I help You?" He said, "Only one thing can cure Me: the foot dust of My devotees." So then Nārada went to Rukmiṇī and Satyabhāmā and the queens, and said, "Oh, Kṛṣṇa has a headache, and the only thing that can cure Him is His devotees' foot dust, please give your foot dust." They said, "(..) No. We cannot put our foot dust on our husband's head." Why? Because in the married relationship, there's maryādā. There's maryādā, so it's not included in the pure line of rāga, rāgātmika, it's that's not a pure rāga. So they said, "We cannot, it's against dharma for the wife to put her foot dust on her husband's head." So then he came back to Kṛṣṇa. Kṛṣṇa said, "Oh Nārada, ask the gopīs of Vṛndāvana." So then Nārada, he went to Vṛndāvana and said to the gopīs, "Kṛṣṇa is suffering with a headache, and the only thing that can cure Him is foot dust of His devotees." So then the gopīs, they took the dust of Vraja. It was the dust of Vraja, and they rubbed it on their feet, and they said, "Nārada, take this." They're rubbing the dust of Vraja on their feet and giving it to Nārada. Nārada said, "Aren't you worried that you go to hell for this?" Gopīs said, "We may go to hell, but let Kṛṣṇa be happy." This is Vraja-gopīs' mood.

[…]

So this bhāva of the gopīs is in that dust. So then Nārada brought that dust to Dvārakā. And then Kṛṣṇa, He took that dust, and He put it on His head. And He felt some relief, because the headache was not really like a migraine. It was actually separation. He was feeling separation from Rādhikā and the Vraja-gopīs.

source.title: 2022.02.09 Sri Madhvacharya Tirobhava Tithi

more.quote: All the saints and sages in India wear tilaka. Sometimes it's slightly different shapes or colors, so... But if you see a temple of Viṣṇu, on the roof of the temple they have this shape. So, this tilaka signifies that my body is a temple and inside this temple along with my ātmā, my soul, is Paramātmā, God is there. When we see another person also wearing tilaka, it reminds us, "Oh, God is there."

content.content: After sitting on a clean ⟦āsana⟧ (seat), pour Ganges water into the ⟦pañca-pātra⟧. In the absence of Ganges water, put fresh water in the ⟦pañca-pātra⟧. Then, remembering the Ganges and other sacred rivers, touch this water, and chant the ⟦tīrtha-āvāhana-mantra⟧.

Use this water and ⟦gopī-candana⟧ to form a paste in the left hand. Then, with the twelve ⟦mantras⟧ beginning with ⟦oṁ keśavāya namaḥ⟧, apply ⟦tilaka⟧ to the twelve different parts of the body, beginning with the forehead, by drawing the ⟦ūrdhva-puṇḍra⟧ (two vertical lines) representing the temple of ⟦Śrī Hari⟧.

Starting from the centre of the eyebrows, form two vertical lines on the forehead that reach up to the beginning of the hairline. There must be a clean space in the middle of the ⟦ūrdhva-puṇḍra⟧. From just below the centre of the eyebrows extending to three-quarters of the way down the nose is called the ⟦nāsāmūla⟧. [This is where one forms the shape of a tulasī leaf.] The ⟦mantra⟧ to invoke remembrance of the twelve names of the Lord (⟦dvādaśa-nāma-smaraṇa-mantra⟧) is as follows:

content.sanskrit:
lalāṭe keśavaṁ dhyāyen
nārāyaṇam athodare
vakṣaḥ-sthale mādhavaṁ tu
govindaṁ kaṇṭha-kūpake

viṣṇuṁ ca dakṣiṇe kukṣau
bāhau ca madhusūdanam
trivikramaṁ kandhare tu
vāmanaṁ vāma-pārśvake

śrīdharaṁ vāma-bāhau tu
hṛṣīkeśaṁ ca kandhare
pṛṣṭhe tu padmanābhaṁ ca
kaṭyāṁ dāmodaraṁ nyaset

tat prakṣālana-toyaṁ tu
vāsudevāya mūrdhani
content.translation: When one marks the forehead with tilaka, one must remember Keśava. When one marks the lower abdomen, one must remember Nārāyaṇa. When marking the chest, one should remember Mādhava, and when marking the hollow of the neck one should remember Govinda. Viṣṇu should be remembered while marking the right side of the belly, and Madhusūdana should be remembered when marking the right arm. Trivikrama should be remembered when marking the right shoulder, and Vāmana should be remembered when marking the left side of the belly. Śrīdhara should be remembered while marking the left arm, and Hṛṣīkeśa should be remembered when marking the left shoulder. Padmanābha and Dāmodara should be remembered when marking the upper and lower back, and Vāsudeva should be remembered when marking the top of the head.

content.content: In accordance with the aforementioned ⟦smaraṇa-mantra⟧, chant the following ⟦mantras⟧ while touching each part of the body, either while applying the ⟦tilaka⟧ mark or after the ⟦tilaka⟧ has already been applied:
Drop a spoonful of water from the ⟦pañca-pātra⟧ into the hand, to mix with the remnant ⟦gopī-candana⟧. Wipe the ⟦candana⟧ on top of the head, while chanting ⟦oṁ vāsudevāya namaḥ⟧.
Note: ⟦Tilaka⟧ paste is to be freshly made each time. Do not apply ⟦Tilaka⟧ in the bathroom.
A pujari who chants twelve names of ⟦Vishnu⟧ always remembers only ⟦Rādhārani⟧.

subsections.title: Performing Ācamana, sipping water for purification

content.content: After applying ⟦tilaka⟧, one should perform ācamana. ⟦Vaiṣṇava⟧ ācamana is of two kinds: ordinary (⟦sādhāraṇa⟧) and specific (⟦viśeṣa⟧). Before performing any devotional activity, ordinary ācamana will suffice. However, at the time of bathing the deity or at the time of ⟦pūjā⟧, ⟦viśeṣa-ācamana⟧ is to be performed.
Sādhāraṇa-ācamana
Drop a spoonful of water [from the ⟦pañca-pātra⟧, or ācamana cup] into the centre of the palm of the right hand (known as the ⟦brāhma-tīrtha⟧) and chant

content.sanskrit: oṁ keśavāya namaḥ

content.content: Sip a little of the water [from the end of the palm] and throw the rest to the ground.
Purify the right hand [by dropping a new spoonful of water in the palm of the right hand and then throwing that water to the ground].
Repeat the above process of ācamana, this time while chanting

content.sanskrit: oṁ nārāyaṇāya namaḥ

content.content: and then again while chanting

content.sanskrit: oṁ mādhavāya namaḥ

content.content: Viśeṣa-ācamana
Always perform ācamana before entering the Deity room to worship the Lord.

With an ⟦ācamana-pātra⟧ filled with water clean both hands by sprinkling them with water; holding the ācamana spoon in your left hand, pour a few drops into the right palm. While looking at the water chant the appropriate ⟦mantra⟧ and then silently sip the water from the base of the right thumb (the ⟦brāhma-tīrtha⟧). The procedure for basic ācamana consists of the first three steps below. If time and circumstances permit, you may perform the complete ācamana:

items.label: ⟦oṁ keśavāya namaḥ⟧
items.value: sip water from the ⟦brāhma-tīrtha⟧ of your right hand.

items.label: ⟦oṁ nārāyaṇāya namaḥ⟧
items.value: sip water from the ⟦brāhma-tīrtha⟧ of your right hand.

items.label: ⟦oṁ mādhavāya namaḥ⟧
items.value: sip water from the ⟦brāhma-tīrtha⟧ of your right hand.

items.label: ⟦oṁ govindāya namaḥ⟧
items.value: sprinkle water on your right hand.

items.label: ⟦oṁ viṣṇave namaḥ⟧
items.value: sprinkle water on your left hand.

items.label: ⟦oṁ madhusūdanāya namaḥ⟧
items.value: touch your right cheek with the fingers of your right hand.

items.label: ⟦oṁ trivikramāya namaḥ⟧
items.value: touch your left cheek with the fingers of your right hand.

items.label: ⟦oṁ vāmanāya namaḥ⟧
items.value: wipe above your upper lip with the base of your right thumb.

items.label: ⟦oṁ śrīdharāya namaḥ⟧
items.value: wipe below your lower lip with the base of your right thumb.

items.label: ⟦oṁ dāmodarāya namaḥ⟧
items.value: sprinkle water on the top of your head.

content.content: While chanting the following ⟦mantras⟧, perform the hand motions:

items.label: ⟦oṁ vāsudevāya namaḥ⟧
items.value: touch your upper and lower lips with the tips of the fingers of your right hand.

items.label: ⟦oṁ saṅkarṣaṇāya namaḥ⟧
items.value: touch your right nostril with your right thumb and forefinger.

items.label: ⟦oṁ pradyumnāya namaḥ⟧
items.value: touch your left nostril with your right thumb and forefinger.

items.label: ⟦oṁ aniruddhāya namaḥ⟧
items.value: touch your right eye with your right thumb and ring finger.

items.label: ⟦oṁ puruṣottamāya namaḥ⟧
items.value: touch your left eye with your right thumb and ring finger.

items.label: ⟦oṁ adhokṣajāya namaḥ⟧
items.value: touch your right ear with your right thumb and forefinger.

items.label: ⟦oṁ nṛsiṁhāya namaḥ⟧
items.value: touch your left ear with your right thumb and forefinger.

items.label: ⟦oṁ acyutāya namaḥ⟧
items.value: touch your navel with your right thumb and little finger.

items.label: ⟦oṁ janārdanāya namaḥ⟧
items.value: touch your heart with the palm of your right hand.

items.label: ⟦oṁ upendrāya namaḥ⟧
items.value: touch your head with all the finger tips of your right hand.

items.label: ⟦oṁ haraye namaḥ⟧
items.value: touch your right upper arm with the fingertips of your left hand.

items.label: ⟦oṁ kṛṣṇāya namaḥ⟧
items.value: touch your left upper arm with the fingertips of your right hand.

content.content: Now chant the following ⟦mantra⟧ from the ⟦Ṛig Veda⟧ while showing the ⟦praṇāma-mudrā⟧ (palms together in front of your heart):

content.sanskrit:
oṁ tad viṣṇoḥ paramaṁ padaṁ
sadā paśyanti sūrayaḥ
divīva cakṣur-ātatam

tad viprāso vipanyavo
jāgṛvaṁ saḥ samindhate
viṣṇor yat paramaṁ padam
content.translation: Just as those with ordinary vision see the sun's rays in the sky, so the wise and learned devotees always see the supreme abode of Lord Vishnu. Because those highly praise-worthy and spiritually awake brāhmaṇas can see that abode, they can also reveal it to others. [Rig Veda Samhita]
content.wbw: oṁ — sacred syllable oṁ; tad — that; viṣṇoḥ — of Lord Viṣṇu; paramaṁ — supreme; padaṁ — abode; sadā — always; paśyanti — see; sūrayaḥ — wise and learned devotees; divīva — as in the sky; cakṣur-ātatam — the rays visible to ordinary sight; tad — that abode; viprāso — brāhmaṇas; vipanyavo — highly praiseworthy; jāgṛvaṁ — spiritually awake; saḥ — they; samindhate — reveal to others; viṣṇor — of Lord Viṣṇu; yat — which; paramaṁ — supreme; padam — abode.

content.content: The pūjārī should arrive no later than 3:20 a.m.
Perform ⟦Viśeṣa-ācamana⟧ (full ācamana)
Make up 1 tray with: Sweets, sweet rice, cup water, cup milk. Note: place tulasī on each preparation.
Make up āratī tray with: Incense, ghee lamp, flowers, handkerchief, water, cotton stick for perfume oil.

content.quote: At that time in the early morning, the mañjarīs, they were awake almost the whole night, but just towards the end of the night, they lie down on the—in the courtyard, just outside the kuñja. And then suddenly, (..) Maidservant wakes up and looks around because she's afraid, "Oh, did I oversleep? Did I miss my service?" And then she looks around, sees, "Oh, others are still resting, Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa are still sleeping." Sigh. Relief. "I thought—for a moment I was very anxious, but now I see there's still time." So then that devotee is remembering his spiritual form, will get up and go and wake up Gurudeva. Understand? That means wake up another sakhī, another other mañjarīs who are there. And then go to see, uṭho, nidrā chāḍi’ uṭha jīva, "Oh, my life and soul, wake up." And they'll go, and they look inside: "Oh, in this beautiful kuñja-bhavana, this pavilion of flowers in the forest of Vṛndāvana on the bank of Yamunā, see Śrī Śrī Rādhā-Śyāmasundara resting there."

source.title: The Story of Nachiketu, Vibhāvarī-Śeṣa with Explanation - 2024-04-07 - Sri Prem Prayojan

more.quote: Oh Kṛṣṇa, please wake up and cast Your merciful glance upon the world. "And when by Your glance You wake up the world, wake up in my heart summaṅgala-rati, very auspicious rati, that is bhāva." The appearance of the divine sentiment of love for Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa. So if you will undergo the inconvenience and austerity to wake up very early every morning and pray, "Oh my Lord, please wake up, open Your eyes, glance upon me, and wake up the rati in my heart," every day, every week, every month, every year, for years and years, what will happen? One day Kṛṣṇa will say, "Okay." He will awaken. "You asked Me so many times, you woke up so early every day for so many years, and you begged Me for this, take." And Kṛṣṇa will give, and then you can hear the birds are singing, cuckoo birds are calling, peacocks are calling, and the sweet nectarine beautiful atmosphere of Vraja, where Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa awaken.

source.title: Who really knows Srimad-Bhagavatam, Sri Prem Prayojan Prabhu in Barcelona, 24.07.2014

more.quote:
In the morning, when we wake up our deities,

[…]

You have to wake up and you touch the feet and wake, "Oh, my dear Ṭhākurajī, please wake up and glance at me with Your auspicious glance. And by that glance, wake up my ecstatic love for You."

more.quote: So first of all, we bow down to Guru. And by his mercy, by his permission, we approach Gaurāṅga. And by the mercy of Gaurāṅga, when we bow down to his līlā, then internally, we have a sphūrti, or the awakening of the realization of Radha Krishna's līlā. When they explained to you, is called bhajana-cāturya. Cāturya means cunningness, cleverness, skill. Many persons, they cannot realize Radha and Krishna because they don't have skill. They don't know the art of how to do bhajana. So the art of how to enter into these confidential pastimes is hinted at here. First, remember Guru, the spiritual master. By his mercy, remember Gaurāṅga in the early morning. When Gaurāṅga Mahāprabhu is waking up in the morning, tears are flowing from his eyes. Why? Because he's remembering how Radha and Krishna are waking up in the morning. So Gaura-līlā is called udbodhaka-līlā. Udbodhaka-līlā means the pastime that awakens your realization of Radha and Krishna's pastimes. So don't try to go directly to Radha and Krishna. First remember Guru, then remember Gaurāṅga, Caitanya Mahāprabhu. And then by his mercy, his mercy will awaken the remembrance of Radha Krishna.

source.title: Mangala Arati - 2025-05-24 - Sri Prem Prayojan

content.content: Prayers to be chanted upon entering the Deity room
Remaining outside the Deity room, ring the bell.
Reciting following verses, pray to the Lord to awaken.

content.sanskrit:
so 'sāv adabhra-karuṇo bhagavān vivṛddha-
prema-smitena nayanāmburuhaṁ vijṛmbhan
utthāya viśva-vijayāya ca no viṣādaṁ
mādhvyā girāpanayatāt puruṣaḥ purāṇaḥ
content.translation: Śrī Bhagavān, who is supreme and primeval, is unlimitedly merciful. I pray that He bless me with His smiling glance by opening His lotus eyes. He can uplift the entire cosmic creation and remove our grief and sorrow with the sweet words of instruction emanating from His lotus mouth. [SB 3.9.25]
content.wbw: so — He; 'sāv — that Lord; adabhra-karuṇo — unlimitedly merciful; bhagavān — Śrī Bhagavān; vivṛddha- — fully blossoming; prema-smitena — with a loving smile; nayanāmburuhaṁ — His lotus eyes; vijṛmbhan — opening wide; utthāya — rising; viśva-vijayāya — to uplift the entire cosmic creation; ca — and; no — our; viṣādaṁ — grief and sorrow; mādhvyā — sweet; girāpanayatāt — may He remove with words; puruṣaḥ — the Supreme Person; purāṇaḥ — primeval.

content.sanskrit:
deva prapannārti-hara prasādaṁ kuru keśava
avalokana-dānena bhūyo māṁ parayācyuta
content.translation: Keśava, O infallible one, O remover of the distress of the surrendered souls, kindly bestow Your mercy upon me by again awarding me with Your transcendental glance.
content.wbw: deva — O Lord; prapannārti-hara — O remover of the distress of the surrendered souls; prasādaṁ — mercy; kuru — kindly bestow; keśava — O Keśava; avalokana-dānena — by granting a glance; bhūyo — again; māṁ — upon me; parayācyuta — transcendental, O Acyuta.

content.sanskrit:
jaya jaya kṛpamaya jagatera nātha
sarva jagatere koro śubha-dṛṣṭī-pāta
content.translation: O Bhagavān! All glories, all glories unto You, O merciful Lord of the universe, please cast Your auspicious glance upon all the worlds.

content.content: Then knock on the door and enter the Deity room.
Turn on a soft light and sit down on the ⟦āsana⟧.
Perform ⟦Sādhāraṇa-ācamana⟧ (ordinary ācamana) and, while ringing the bell, proceed to the place where ⟦Srī Gurudeva⟧ is resting. Awaken him by touching his feet and chant the following prayers.
Prayers in Deity's room
Touching the feet of ⟦Śrī Gurudev⟧, awaken Him by chanting:

content.sanskrit:
uttiṣṭhottiṣṭha śrī guro
tyaja nidrāṁ kṛpāmaya
aing gurave namaḥ
content.translation: O most merciful Gurudeva, please arise, please arise and give up your sleep.
content.wbw: uttiṣṭhottiṣṭha — please arise, please arise; śrī — revered; guro — O Gurudeva; tyaja — give up; nidrāṁ — sleep; kṛpāmaya — most merciful one; aing — bīja-mantra of Sarasvatī; gurave — unto Gurudeva; namaḥ — obeisances.

content.content: Then, touching the feet of ⟦Śrī Gaurāṅga⟧, awaken Him by chanting:

content.sanskrit:
uttiṣṭhottiṣṭha gaurāṅga
jahi nidrāṁ mahāprabho
śubha-dṛṣṭi pradānena
trailokya-maṅgalaṁ kuru
klīng gaurāya svāhā
content.translation: O Gaurāṅga Mahāprabhu, please arise, please arise and give up Your sleep. Please benedict the three worlds with Your auspicious glance.
content.wbw: uttiṣṭhottiṣṭha — please arise, please arise; gaurāṅga — O Gaurāṅga; jahi — give up; nidrāṁ — sleep; mahāprabho — O Mahāprabhu; śubha-dṛṣṭi — auspicious glance; pradānena — by giving; trailokya-maṅgalaṁ — blessing of the three worlds; kuru — please bestow; klīng — bīja-mantra of Kāmadeva (Kṛṣṇa, attraction); gaurāya — to Gaura; svāhā — offering exclamation “svāhā”.

content.content: Next, while touching the lotus feet of ⟦Śrī Rādhā Krsna⟧ awaken Them by chanting:

content.sanskrit:
go-gopa-gokulānanda
yaśodānanda vardhana
uttiṣṭha rādhayā sārddhaṁ
prātar āsīj jagat-pate
śrīng klīng rādhā-kṛṣṇābhyāṁ namaḥ
content.translation: O joy of Gokula, the cowherd boys and the cows; O increaser of Mother Yaśodā's bliss; O Lord of the universe; please arise along with Śrī Rādhā, for it is almost morning.
content.wbw: go-gopa-gokulānanda — O joy of Gokula, the cowherd boys and the cows; yaśodānanda — O increaser of Mother Yaśodā's bliss; vardhana — increaser; uttiṣṭha — please arise; rādhayā — along with Śrī Rādhā; sārddhaṁ — together with; prātar — in the morning; āsīj — it is almost; jagat-pate — O Lord of the universe; śrīng — bīja-mantra of Śrī, Lakṣmī and Rādhā; klīng — bīja-mantra of Kāmadeva, Kṛṣṇa, and divine attraction; rādhā-kṛṣṇābhyāṁ — to Śrī Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa; namaḥ — obeisances.

content.content: Afterward, meditate that these personalities have risen and taken their seat on the altar.
(Physically place the Deities on the altar if They were removed from there the previous night and placed in a bed.)
Carefully replace the Chota Deities on the altar, put crown on Deities.
Clean and cover the bed.

subsections.title: Washing the mouth of the Lord

content.content: Now, while chanting the following ⟦mantras⟧, one should first offer ācamana (water for cleansing the mouth) to ⟦Sri Guru⟧ and the deity. Then offer a twig for cleaning the teeth (⟦danta-kāṣṭha⟧), and again ācamana:

content.sanskrit:
idaṁ ācamanīyaṁ aing gurave namaḥ
idaṁ ācamanīyaṁ klīng gaurāya svāhā
idaṁ ācamanīyaṁ śrīng klīng rādhā-kṛṣṇābhyāṁ namaḥ

content.content: Note: Ācamana is offered by tipping a spoonful of water from the ⟦pañca-pātra⟧ into an empty container (⟦visarjanīya-pātra⟧), while ringing the bell and saying the respective ⟦mantra⟧.

content.sanskrit:
eṣa danta-kāṣṭhaḥ aing gurave namaḥ
eṣa danta-kāṣṭhaḥ klīng gaurāya svāhā
eṣa danta-kāṣṭhaḥ śrīng klīng rādhā-kṛṣṇābhyāṁ namaḥ

content.content: The above ⟦mantras⟧ signify the offering of a twig for cleaning the teeth (⟦danta-kāṣṭha⟧). This item is offered by mind rather than by offering the actual article. Generally, in the absence of any item, one may meditate on the particular item and, while saying the appropriate ⟦mantra⟧, offer water from the ⟦pañca-pātra⟧ into the throw-out pot.
Now offer ācamana like before, but 12 times. (3 times is also acceptable.)

subsections.title: Cleaning the Deities and the altar

content.content: Wipe the face, hands and feet of each Deity with a clean cloth. After removing old garlands, tulasī leaves and flowers, clean the altar and then purify one's hands. Offer tulasī and decorate each Deity with the appropriate crown, flute and ornaments while chanting Their appropriate ⟦mūla-mantra⟧. Then perform ⟦maṅgala-ārati⟧.
Replace crowns and ⟦Kṛṣṇa⟧'s staff and water cups. Make bed. Place out sitting mats for ⟦bhoga⟧ offering and clean offering tables.

content.quote: But the problem is that Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa cannot go home being decorated in the sambhoga-cihna. So they'll have to be, (..) (..) removed. And that's why the pujārī in maṅgala-ārati is coming with a water and a cloth. So first she puts the water in the conch, that means the maidservants are coming and putting some, (..) fresh, fragrant water on the bodies of Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa, and taking the cloth and wiping away the sambhoga-cihna. But as they wipe away As this As these cihna are the signs of sambhoga meeting, then as they're being wiped away, that means it's as if they are erasing the pastime itself. And it's awakening the vipralambha-bhāva. When the sambhoga-cihna is wiped away, when meeting is wiped away, then you are left with separation. This is the bhāva of maṅgala-ārati. So the devotees are watching the ārati and seeing the offering of the water, the offering of the cloth like this, and the nectar of the union is being wiped away, and the pain of separation is rising up in the heart.

more.quote:
Some of the maidservants, they're taking some fragrant water and very soft cloth, and dipping it, and wiping away the various cosmetics from the faces of Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa because Kṛṣṇa has Rādhikā’s lip gloss here, and some kājala, black kājala from Her eyes on His lips, and some cosmetics, some candana, kastūrī, and the musk and so on is smeared on the body of Rādhikā, so they're coming and with a cloth and wiping away, just like the pūjārī in the maṅgala-ārati is offering some water, and then taking a cloth and offering cloth and cleaning like this. This is the inner meaning of (..) the āratī. Another maidservant takes a dīpa and does āratī because āratī means that which brings auspiciousness. So they're thinking, “Oh, I am offering āratī to Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa, They will now get back to Their home without being caught, there should be no problems. No difficulties should come in Their life, and They should quickly again meet without any obstacles.” When a person offers āratī in a sweet mood, it means, “May whatever difficulties are there in your life, I'll let me take all of those difficulties on my head, and let you be free from any problems.” And this is the loving mood.

Some maidservants are then fanning with a cāmara. So in this cāmara, there are so many hairs, right? So these hairs, these are like the prāṇa. There are 72,000 nāḍīs in the body, so the hairs of the cāmara are like 72,000 nāḍīs with the prāṇa, that means, “Oh, worshipping Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa with all their prāṇa.” They're not thinking metaphysically, only this is (..) a bhāva that they're serving with all their prāṇa, just to please Rādhā. Their only happiness is lies in Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa’s happiness, and Kṛṣṇa’s happiness lies in Rādhārāṇī’s happiness, so we'll just focus on Her mainly. If Rādhikā is happy, Kṛṣṇa is happy, so we focus the service on Śrīmatī Rādhikā.

source.title: Meaning of Mangala Arati - 2021-07-23 - Sri Prem Prayojan

more.quote: And outside, a gentle breeze is blowing and causing the lotus flowers in the Yamunā and in the lakes to tremble, and carrying (..) their fragrance. So now Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa outside, and just now they'll have to return to their homes, but just to make sure that there's no obstacle, that there's no hitch, that they don't get seen or discovered on the way, then Lalitā-sakhī comes, and Lalitā-sakhī is doing ārati. Ārati means, because a general person who is in aiśvarya, they do ārati to the Deity, they have so many ideas: Supreme Lord is the creator of the universe, earth, water, fire, air, and ether, so I'm offering the incense because fragrance is the quality of earth, and I'm offering the dīpa because that is fire, and water, and like this, and air with the fan, like So this is people think about ārati in this sense. But in the Vedic culture, ārati means that we are performing this auspicious ritual, that whatever difficulty or problem may come in your life, may you not face that, let it come to me, and not to you. So, for example, like Mātā Yaśodā offers ārati to Kṛṣṇa when He comes back in the evening from taking the cows to graze, you think Mātā Yaśodā is saying, "I am worshiping You with all the elements"? So try to understand that ārati as a loving dimension of may you be happy and let all whatever calamity may fall upon you, I'll take it on my head. So in this way, Lalitā-sakhī and all the sakhīs, Lalitā-sakhī is leading the ārati, and this is maṅgala-ārati.

source.title: 2019.12.22 Meanings Of Japa And Mangala Arati

more.quote: It means may this auspicious maṅgala-ārati awaken in the hearts of the devotees. We are not practicing Kṛṣṇa consciousness to be forever in a state of no anubhāva, realization, anubhūti. We are searching for realization. And so in maṅgala-ārati we're praying, "(..) Oh Guru, Oh Gaurāṅga, Oh Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa, sprinkle Your mercy upon me that this beautiful scene of Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa's waking in the morning, the maṅgala-ārati, will rise up in my heart."

source.title: Sri Prem Prayojan - 2019-12-22 - Meanings of Japa and Mangala Arati

more.quote: So, soon Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa will have to secretly return to Their homes. So the mañjarīs bring the, all the paraphernalia for ārati, and Lalitā-sakhī performs the ārati ceremony. Yes. They bring all the paraphernalia. You see, the sakhīs, they don't do that kind of work, the mañjarīs, the maidservants do all the small things. (..) And she's offering ārati, (..) and we are experiencing this ārati in morning. The meaning of ārati is to make maṅgala, auspiciousness. In other words, "Oh, Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa, we are praying, and You can return to Your homes without anyone catching You and finding out what happened, and there'll be no obstacles, no problems." And who is offering the ārati and watching the ārati, they feel, "In my life, if I have any good karma, I am offering it all to You, so that You will not experience any suffering at all. Let the suffering come to me, but not to You." This is the meaning of ārati. Of course, (^)Rādhā, Kṛṣṇa, gopīs, they have no karma, but because Their pastime is the nara-vat, human-like pastimes, They don't know They are God or Goddess or anything. They play—it is a līlā—They play like humans. So they are thinking in this way. Oh, she's fanning with the cāmara. So the cāmara, it has thousands and thousands of hairs. And gopīs are thinking, "(..) Oh Kṛṣṇa, oh Rādhikā, we are serving You with our 72,000 nāḍīs. 72,000 prāṇas, we are worshipping You, that's our cāmara."

content.content: 4:10 a.m. Offer ⟦bhoga⟧ (follow the ⟦bhoga⟧ offering procedure).

content.content: Guru
Then invite ⟦Srī Gurudeva⟧ to his resting place with the following ⟦mantra⟧:

content.sanskrit:
āgaccha viśrāma-sthānaṁ
sva-gaṇaiḥ saha śrī-guro
aing gurave namaḥ
content.translation: O Gurudeva, kindly come to your resting place along with all your associates.

content.content: Chant ⟦mantras⟧ for forgiveness (Prayers Begging Forgiveness for Offences).

content.quote: Then they made a deity of Kātyāyanī from clay on the bank of the river, here. And they offered 16 articles. And with every article, they were thinking of Kṛṣṇa. When they offered the incense, "O Kātyāyanī-devī, we're offering you this fragrant incense, please offer to our nostrils the fragrance of Śrī Kṛṣṇa." "O Devī, we're offering this dīpas, these lights to you, please give us the shining light of the eyes of Kṛṣṇa." Like this, with every article that they're offering, they were begging Kātyāyanī to fulfill their desire to meet Kṛṣṇa.

source.title: Chīr Ghaṭa - 2024-10-25 - Sri Prem Prayojan

more.quote:
Rules help us in our spiritual life; if we neglect them, we lose something. But if you just follow rules without knowing why you're doing it, it will also not have a good effect. So everything that we do in bhakti, whether it's putting on tilaka, or bowing down, or offering incense and flowers to Kṛṣṇa, everything has a very deep meaning, so it should not be done mechanically.

[…]

So what benefit is there? If you think, "I'm not going to make any offering. I'll just put some money in the machine." You have to do the bhakti yourself. But doing it, don't be like that machine. One's heart has to be involved in that offering. So the offering has a very deep meaning.

source.title: Sri Prem Prayojan - 2019-06-23 - Ishtha-Goshthi 2

more.quote: Along with the dīkṣā-mantra, the guru gives some process of arcana, of worship of the deity. And this consists of several things: waking the deity in the morning, putting deity to rest in evening, and offering prasādam, and give the seats, idam āsanam, sprinkling like this, and offer them seats, wash their feet, wash their hands and mouth, and offer them prasādam, etc., as if you're serving a guest in your home, very beautiful.

source.title: Gaura Arati p.1 [eng]

content.content: Outside the Deity room (Pujari room) perform ācamana and offer obeisances to your spiritual master.
Pujari collects the necessary paraphernalia for the worship of Deities.
To avoid interrupting the worship, see to it that the following items are present before beginning:
Enter in the Deity room, clean the area where you will do the worship and place an ⟦asana⟧ on the floor.
Carry all required paraphernalia into the Deity room.
Place the ⟦asana⟧ in position for performing the worship and, while kneeling, with joined palms (⟦pranama-mudra⟧) chant:

content.sanskrit:
pṛthvi tvayā dhṛtā lokā
devi tvaṃ viṣṇunā dhṛtā
tvaṃ ca dhāraya māṃ nityaṃ
pavitraṃ kuru cāsanam
content.translation: O Mother Earth, O goddess, you support all the world's people, and Lord Visnu sustains you; please be merciful today and support me as I sit to worship the Lord.
content.wbw: pṛthvi — O Mother Earth; tvayā — by you; dhṛtā — supported; lokā — the worlds; devi — O goddess; tvaṃ — you; viṣṇunā — by Lord Viṣṇu; dhṛtā — are supported; tvaṃ — you; ca — and; dhāraya — support; māṃ — me; nityaṃ — always; pavitraṃ — pure; kuru — make; cāsanam — and the seat.

content.content: While thinking of your spiritual master sitting on an ⟦asana⟧ in position for performing the worship, sit on your own ⟦asana⟧.
Arrange the items in such a way that you can easily reach them without touching offered to un-offered items.

Place the bell (on a plate) to your left and place the bathing conch on a stand so you can easily lift and replace it several times. The waterpot, flowers, ⟦candana⟧, and tulasī leaves should be within easy reach.

Use the throw-out pot (⟦visarjanīya-pātra⟧) for offered ācamana and ⟦arghya⟧, or you may pour these liquids into the bathing receptacle (⟦snāna-pātra⟧) if it is a receptacle which has a drain. You may use a second ⟦visarjanīya-pātra⟧ for offered flower petals, cotton swabs, etc.
Bathing towels should be placed on a tray, table or the altar, not on your lap or directly on the floor. This applies to all paraphernalia; nothing should be placed on the lower cloth or the floor.

subsections.title: Requesting the Spiritual Master's and Previous Ācāryas' Blessings (guru-paṅkti-namaskāra)

content.content: Preliminary Worship
Begin the ⟦arcana⟧ of ⟦Śrī Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa⟧ by seeking the permission and mercy of ⟦Sri Guru⟧ and ⟦Śrī Gaurāṅga⟧:
Chant:

content.sanskrit:
Tvaṁ gopikā vṛṣa-raves tanayāntike ‘si...
Oṁ ajñāna-timirāndhasya...
Nāma-śreṣṭhaṁ manum api śacī-putram atra svarūpaṁ...
Vāñchā-kalpa-tarubhyaś ca...
Maha mantra

content.content: ⟦Śrī Gurudeva⟧ is a confidential servant and an intimate friend (⟦sakhī⟧) of ⟦Śrī Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa⟧. ⟦Gurudeva⟧ is engaged in the direct service of ⟦Śrī Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa⟧. Meditating like this and remembering one's incapability, perform ⟦arcana⟧.
Draw the attention of your spiritual master by placing flowers before him while chanting

content.sanskrit: eṣa puṣpāñjaliḥ aing gurave namaḥ

content.content: Then, meditating on your spiritual master's service to the previous ⟦ācāryas⟧, show the ⟦praṇāma-mudrā⟧ (joined palms) and pray for his blessings to assist in the worship of the Lord.
Offer ⟦praṇāma⟧ to the ⟦guru-paramparā⟧, situated on the altar, then recite:

content.sanskrit: aing gurave namaḥ
content.translation: I offer obeisances to my spiritual master.
content.wbw: aing — bīja-mantra of Sarasvatī; gurave — to the spiritual master; namaḥ — obeisances.

content.sanskrit: aing parama-gurave namaḥ
content.translation: I offer obeisances to my grand spiritual master.
content.wbw: aing — bīja-mantra of Sarasvatī; parama-gurave — to my grand spiritual master; namaḥ — obeisances.

content.sanskrit: aing parameṣṭhi gurave namaḥ
content.translation: I offer obeisances to my great grand spiritual master.
content.wbw: aing — bīja-mantra of Sarasvatī; parameṣṭhi — great-grand; gurave — to the spiritual master; namaḥ — obeisances.

content.sanskrit: aing śrī guru-paramparāyai namaḥ
content.translation: I offer obeisances to śrī guru-paramparā.
content.wbw: aing — bīja-mantra of Sarasvatī; śrī — glorious, revered; guru-paramparāyai — to śrī guru-paramparā; namaḥ — obeisances.

content.sanskrit: oṁ sarva-gurūttamāya śrī kṛṣṇa-caitanyāya namaḥ
content.translation: I offer obeisances to the topmost of all gurus, Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya.
content.wbw: oṁ — sacred syllable oṁ; sarva-gurūttamāya — to the topmost of all gurus; śrī — revered; kṛṣṇa-caitanyāya — to Kṛṣṇa Caitanya; namaḥ — obeisances.

content.content: Wash your hands with water from the waterpot.
Sprinkle the flowers with ⟦Samānya-arghya⟧ (holy rivers) water while chanting:

content.sanskrit: oṁ astrāya phaṭ

oṁ puṣpe puṣpe mahā-puṣpe
su-puṣpe puṣpa-sambhave
puṣpe cayavākīrṇe ca
huṁ phaṭ svāhā
content.translation: O flowers, O great and auspicious flowers who have appeared from a budding creeper, may you be purified.
content.wbw: oṁ — sacred syllable oṁ; puṣpe — O flowers; puṣpe — O flowers; mahā-puṣpe — O great flowers; su-puṣpe — O auspicious flowers; puṣpa-sambhave — who have appeared from a flower; puṣpe — O flowers; cayavākīrṇe — arisen from a budding creeper; ca — and; huṁ — protective bīja-mantra; phaṭ — protective exclamation; svāhā — offering exclamation "svāhā".

content.content: Sprinkle all the paraphernalia lightly with ⟦samānya-arghya⟧ water while chanting:

content.sanskrit: oṁ astrāya phaṭ

content.content: Purifying the bodily elements by identifying oneself as the eternal servant of the servant of Lord Kṛṣṇa

Before ⟦arcana⟧, one purifies oneself by thinking: "By constitution I am an eternal servant of ⟦Śrī Kṛṣṇa⟧, but by some misfortune, I became averse to Him since time immemorial. Having thus identified myself as a material body in this illusory existence and having been trapped in this repeated cycle of birth and death, I was burning in the blazing fire of the threefold miseries. However, by great fortune -- that is, by the mercy of ⟦Sri Guru⟧ -- I have come to understand my identity as a minute, atomic spiritual particle, an eternal servant of ⟦Śrī Kṛṣṇa⟧, completely aloof from the gross and subtle bodies. Now, by the order of ⟦Sri Gurudeva⟧, under his shelter, I have obtained the fortune of serving ⟦Śrī Guru-Gaurāṅga⟧ and ⟦Śrī Rādhā-Vinoda-Bihārījī⟧."

content.sanskrit:
nāhaṁ vipro na ca nara-patir nāpi vaiśyo na śūdro
nāhaṁ varṇī na ca gṛha-patir no vana-stho yatir vā
kintu prodyan-nikhila-paramānanda-pūrṇāmṛtābdher
gopī-bhartuḥ pada-kamālāyor dāsa-dāsānudāsaḥ
content.translation: I am not a brāhmaṇa, kṣatriya, vaiśya or śūdra, nor am I a brahmacārī, gṛhastha, vānaprastha or sannyāsī. Being transcendental to this gross and subtle body, I am the servant of the servant of the servant of the lotus feet of the master of the gopīs, Śrī Kṛṣṇa, who is the ultimate shelter of everyone, full of transcendental bliss and an ocean of unlimited nectar. [Padyāvalī 74]
content.wbw: nāhaṁ — I am not; vipro — a brāhmaṇa; na — not; ca — and; nara-patir — a kṣatriya; nāpi — nor; vaiśyo — a vaiśya; na — not; śūdro — a śūdra; nāhaṁ — I am not; varṇī — a brahmacārī; na — nor; ca — and; gṛha-patir — a gṛhastha; no — nor; vana-stho — a vānaprastha; yatir — a sannyāsī; vā — or; kintu — but; prodyan-nikhila-paramānanda-pūrṇāmṛtābdher — of the ocean of nectar, full of rising, unlimited transcendental bliss; gopī-bhartuḥ — of the master of the gopīs; pada-kamālāyor — of the lotus feet; dāsa-dāsānudāsaḥ — the servant of the servant of the servant.

content.quote: I am sitting at the lotus feet of my guru. I'm wearing a divyaṁ śrī-hari-mandira-tilakam, beautiful tilaka. Harināma-subhagaṁ, my body is made with sandalwood paste (..) and the holy names, Radheshyam or Gaura Gadadhara or Hare Krishna painted on my body in sandalwood paste. I'm wearing very clean cloth and I'm sitting at the feet of guru and I am overwhelmed with intense enthusiasm to serve. This is called the ātma-jñāna mantra.

more.quote:
But if when you sit down to chant, what do you do? Well, first you do ācamana. Oṁ keśavāya namaḥ, oṁ nārāyaṇāya namaḥ. You do ācamana. And then you pray,

[…]

You do the bhūta-śuddhi mantra. I am not Vaiśya, Kṣatriya, Śūdra, Brāhmaṇa. I am not Brahmacārī, Vānaprastha, Gṛhastha or Sannyāsī. content.sanskrit:
divyaṁ śrī-hari-mandirāḍhya-tilakaṁ kaṇṭhaṁ sumālānvitaṁ
vakṣaḥ śrī-harināma-varṇa-subhagaṁ śrī-khaṇḍa-liptaṁ punaḥ

content.translation: I meditate on myself as being surrendered at the lotus feet of śrī guru and possessing great determination to serve him. I meditate on myself, with my forehead adorned with beautiful tilaka, representing the temple of Śrī Hari. I am wearing a beautiful necklace of tulasī beads. My chest is marked with the holy name and anointed with sandalwood pulp. I am dressed in fine and pure cloth, and within, I am constantly absorbed in ever-fresh spiritual sentiments.

content.content: Note: In brief, before one begins ⟦arcana⟧, one should clean the altar and the paraphernalia. Place the articles in a convenient place. It is important to sanctify the water in the ⟦pañca-pātra⟧ with the ⟦mantra⟧ "⟦gaṅge ca yamune caiva...⟧" and to purify flowers with the ⟦mantra⟧ "⟦puṣpe puṣpe mahā-puṣpe...⟧". ⟦Pādya⟧, ⟦arghya⟧ and ⟦ācamanīya⟧ are usually substituted with pure water from the ⟦pañca-pātra⟧. Similarly, if any item cannot be procured, it can be substituted by meditation and the offering of water from the ⟦pañca-pātra⟧ or conch shell.
While offering the bell a flower petal dipped in ⟦candana⟧, chant:

content.sanskrit: ete gandha-puspe oṁ jaya-dhuani-mantra-matāh svāhā

content.content: Now affix the flower petal to the body of the bell with the ⟦candana⟧. Then ring the bell briefly with your left hand and replace it on the plate, all the while thinking of the bell as a servant of the Lord.
While offering flowers and ⟦candana⟧ to the Lord's bathing conch, chant:

content.sanskrit:
ete gandha-puspe
oṁ hum hum hum namah maha-sankhaya svāhā

content.content: See "⟦Arcana⟧ of ⟦Sri Guru⟧" section.
Then chant the ⟦prema-dhvani⟧ for your spiritual master: ⟦jaya oṁ viṣṇupāda⟧ [name of your spiritual master] ⟦kī jaya⟧.

subsections.title: Worshipping Lord Caitanya and Śrī Śrī Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa with sixteen upacāras (bāhya-pūjā)

content.content: Meditation on Śrī Vṛndāvana-dhāma

content.sanskrit:
tato vṛndāvanaṁ dhyāyet paramānanda-vardhanam
kālindī-jala-kallola- saṅgi-māruta-sevitam
nānā-puṣpa-latā-baddha- vṛkṣa-ṣaṇḍaiś ca maṇḍitam
koṭi-sūrya-samābhāsaṁ vimuktaṁ ṣaṭ-taraṅgakaiḥ
tan-madhye ratna-khacitaṁ svarṇa-siṁhāsanaṁ mahat
content.translation: Meditate on a great golden throne studded with jewels within the divine realm of Śrī Vṛndāvana-dhāma. A place of ever-increasing bliss, Vṛndāvana-dhāma is served by breezes cooled by the touch of the Yamunā's waves and is decorated with various types of flowers, creepers and trees. Its splendour is equal to that of millions of suns, and it is ever free from the six waves of material nature (namely, lust, anger, greed, envy, false ego and illusion).

content.content: Meditation on Śrī Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa

dīvyad-vṛndāraṇya-kalpa-drumādhaḥ
śrīmad-ratnāgāra-siṁhāsana-sthau
śrī-śrī-rādhā-śrīla-govinda-devau
preṣṭhālībhiḥ sevyamānau smarāmi
content.translation: In the shining land of Śrī Vṛndāvana, in a temple composed of jewels, Śrī Rādhā-Govinda are seated on an effulgent throne beneath a kalpa-vṛkṣa tree, accepting service from Their beloved sakhīs. I meditate upon Them. [Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta Ādi-līlā 1.16]

sat-puṇḍarīka-nayanaṁ meghābhaṁ vaidyutāmbaram
dvi-bhujaṁ veṇu-vaktrābjaṁ vana-mālinam īśvaram
divyālaṅkāraṇopetaṁ sakhībhiḥ pariveṣṭitam

content.translation: I meditate on Śrī Kṛṣṇa (seated on the jewelled throne), who possesses beautiful lotus eyes, whose bodily hue resembles that of a fresh raincloud, who wears a yellow silken dhotī, who has two arms, who plays the flute, who wears beautiful forest garlands, who is adorned with glittering ornaments, who is surrounded by the gopīs, who embraces Śrīmatī Rādhikā and whose body is composed of transcendental consciousness and bliss.

pūrṇānanda-kalevaram

content.quote: Actually, when a pūjārī, the priest who is serving the deity, offers any articles to the deity, actually, he should offer the articles first by in the mind. And so, he's thinking, "Oh, in my svarūpa with my guru-rūpa-sakhī, my Gurudeva in Her svarūpa, and I am passing the articles and together we are serving Rādhikā." So when you do ṣoḍaśopacāra-pūjā, worship with 16 articles, each one is done by mind first, and then the actual physical article is done.

more.quote: So, all these phrases like upacāra and pūjā indicate vaidhi-bhakti. Vaidhi-bhakti. There's no pūjā in rāgānuga-bhakti. If someone serves the Deity in rāgānuga-bhakti, it's not called pūjā; it's called sevā. It's different.

content.content: After meditating in this way, chant ⟦Sri Gāndhārvikā-Giridhārī Sri Rādhā-Vinoda-Bihārījī kī jaya⟧. First perform worship within the mind (⟦mānasa-pūjā⟧), and then, with external items, perform worship of the Divine Couple -- in the form of the Deity. Offer each item first to Lord ⟦Śrī Kṛṣṇa⟧, then ⟦Śrīmatī Rādhārānī⟧.
Reception
While ringing a bell, chant:

content.sanskrit: eṣa puṣpāñjali klīng gaurāya svāhā śrīng klīng rādhā-kṛṣṇābhyām namaḥ

content.content: Offer flower petals to Their Lordship's lotus feet.

content.sanskrit:
idaṁ āsanaṁ klīng gaurāya svāhā
śrīng klīng rādhā-kṛṣṇābhyāṁ namaḥ

content.quote: Ucchiṣṭa means remnant. If Gurudeva is eating, then what is left on his plate, this is ucchiṣṭa, and the disciple wants to take the ucchiṣṭa, the remnant of Gurudeva. But the actual desire of taking the ucchiṣṭa is: "Oh, Gurudeva, when will you give me your ucchiṣṭa-sevā, the remnant of your service to Rādhikā?" So, this prayer, śrī-rūpa-mañjarī-karārcita-pāda-padma, is (..) very sweet, because Raghunātha dāsa Gosvāmī is praying for the ucchiṣṭa-sevā of his śikṣā-guru, Rūpa Gosvāmī. It is extraordinarily beautiful and sweet because it is the extremity of ānugatyamayī-sevā, being in ānugatya. Not only to serve under the guidance, but actually to take up the remnant of the very service. So, this is the picture of rūpānuga-bhajana.

content.quote: Śrī Kṛṣṇa Himself had said, "Oh, don't serve Me first, serve your Gurudeva first. Worship your Gurudeva first, and then after that, you can worship Me. If you do this, then there's no doubt you'll attain siddhi, you'll become perfected. But if one does not worship his Gurudeva first, then everything is niṣphala, has no fruit at all." Why? Because we cannot trespass, we cannot force our way into the divine realm. Everything is by permission, by permission only. So first, we seek permission from Gurudeva to serve Gaurāṅga, and then we seek permission from Gaurāṅga to serve Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa. Only when They open the door to divine, (..) divine plane and accept us as Their near and dear one, as Their associate, then we can enter, otherwise not, by our own power it is completely impossible.

more.quote: Guru is direct manifestation of Supreme Lord, and (..) Rūpa Gosvāmī said that all the aṅgas of bhakti can be practiced in relation to Guru also. But there's some vyāvahārika consideration as well. And there'll be some For example, the (..) pūjārī every day, he's undressing the Deity and then giving bath, and but Guru himself is doing all these things. No need for the disciples to the give the shower to Gurudeva and everything (..) Okay, when Mādhavendra Purī was very old, Īśvara Purī had to do these things. But generally speaking, (..) how you would serve the Deity, you will not serve Kṛṣṇa like that. (..) And (..) then there are some considerations that you can put tulasī on Kṛṣṇa's feet, but (..) you cannot even offer tulasī directly to Guru. You can give Gurudeva Kṛṣṇa's mahā-prasāda tulasī, or if (..) the tulasī is not mahā-prasāda, you can put it in Gurudeva's right hand for him to offer to Kṛṣṇa as a service like that. So (..) all the aṅgas of bhakti can be performed in relation to Guru and Vaiṣṇavas, but there's some also depend (..) some nuances. Certain things you can do and not do, or you have to do them in a different way, because Guru is a category, Vaiṣṇava is a category, Kṛṣṇa Mahāprabhu is a category, Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa. Though Mahāprabhu Himself is Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa, but you can serve Him as the Kṛṣṇa Himself, but higher than that is to serve Him as a devotee of Kṛṣṇa, because that's His own mood. Then you're serving Him according to His own mood. So one person will put tulasī (..) you can put tulasī on the feet of Caitanya Mahāprabhu. But in rāgānugā-bhakti, we'll put the tulasī in His right hand, because we serve Him according to His own mood. Just like in Purī, when Mahāprabhu was cleaning the Guṇḍicā temple, one devotee came (..) and poured water on His feet and drank the caraṇāmṛta while He was on the altar of Lord Jagannātha before Lord Jagannātha had arrived there. Mahāprabhu became angry. So inwardly He was pleased, because there's nothing wrong, because He is Kṛṣṇa Himself. That's okay. (..) But He Himself, His mood is, "I am a devotee," and we don't want to (..) disturb that. So Kṛṣṇa wears a peacock feather, but we should not give a peacock feather to Caitanya Mahāprabhu. So (..) and Gurudeva is the sākṣād-dhari, but you don't give Gurudeva a peacock feather or a flute or anything like this. So in principle, the aṅga of bhakti is the same (..) but there are some considerations according to tattva and according to rasa also. Gaura-premānande hari haribol!

more.quote: Now the mantra that we use, this is important. If you have Deity of Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa, but no Gaurāṅga, but you should still think Gaurāṅga is there. We never worship Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa without Mahāprabhu first. And, uh, if you have Gaurāṅga, then you think that Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa is there. And you this, so the mantra is this, you hear: Eṣa puṣpāñjaliḥ klīṁ gaurāya svāhā śrīṁ klīṁ rādhā-kṛṣṇābhyāṁ namaḥ. So this mantra it's there on your sheet. So it's a combined it combines the mantra to Gaura and the man- and mantra to Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa in one. Though you are on the level of vaidhī-bhakti, though we are teaching vaidhī-bhakti, we are teaching the vaidhī-bhakti in such a way that it's one-pointed, it will turn into rāgānugā-bhakti. Because in the in the ordinary vaidhī-bhakti, you do the offering to Gaurāṅga, and a separate offering to Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa. But because we are going one-pointed to Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa and seeing Gaurāṅga as our śikṣā-guru, so we don't make a separate offering. Or you can think that, uh, Mahāprabhu is the rasarāja-mahābhāva-svarūpa, the combined form of Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa when Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa in the prema-vilāsa-vivarta. He's a prema-vilāsa-vivartamayi mūrti. So only one mantra, not separate mantras. That's pure vaidhī-bhakti. So you're doing vaidhī-bhakti, but the vaidhī-bhakti you are learning is exactly focus to enter very smoothly into rāgānugā-bhakti.

content.content: The procedure for offering foodstuffs (⟦bhoga⟧) is the same throughout the day.

The devotee should consider himself fallen and unworthy, not qualified to offer ⟦bhoga⟧ to the Lord, but should pray to ⟦Gurudev⟧, knowing that he is a worthy servant. One should offer ⟦asana⟧ to ⟦Gurudev⟧ and call out to him: "Please offer this ⟦bhoga⟧ to the Deities you worship." (We ask the ⟦Guru⟧ to offer food to ⟦Rādhā⟧ and ⟦Kṛṣṇa⟧, but we do not offer it for him to eat).

Although the ⟦guru⟧ offers food, the disciple, while chanting the ⟦mantras⟧, meditates on being helped by him. The ⟦gaura-mula-mantra⟧ is always chanted along with the ⟦mula-mantra⟧ of ⟦Śrī Śrī Rādhā Kṛṣṇa⟧, even when the ⟦vigraha⟧ of Lord ⟦Caitanya⟧ is not present.
We should offer the ⟦bhoga⟧ with a feeling that ⟦śrī gurudeva⟧ himself is offering the ⟦bhoga⟧ to ⟦Śrīman Mahāprabhu⟧ and ⟦Śrī Śrī Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa⟧.

content.quote:

It's, but it's a very simple thing, and a basic thing. And that is that you do this ceremony first to guru.

[…]

Then you take, and then you offer them: eṣa puṣpāñjaliḥ aiṁ gurave namaḥ. Offer the puṣpāñjali at the feet of Gurudeva. Then you take an āsana. So usually they have like this, some small seats. So then, uh, ringing the bell and place the āsana in front of Gurudeva: idam āsanaṁ aiṁ gurave namaḥ. Then, uh, inviting Gurudeva: āvāhayāmi, that means come, and then sit down, sthāpayāmi, and then welcome: prabhu kṛpayā svāgataṁ kuru. Āvāhayāmi sthāpayāmi prabhu kṛpayā svāgataṁ kuru. content.quote: In rāga-mārga, one has to follow the associates. What is the mood of the sakhīs when they are offering ārati to Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa? You see, even Mother Yaśodā, when Kṛṣṇa returns in the evening from taking the cows to graze, Mother Yaśodā and all the elderly mothers, they also offer ārati to Kṛṣṇa. So it cannot be because they think He's God. So (..) there's another meaning to ārati. Ārati is a reception when you receive someone, you welcome them in this way. But the bhāva of the, when a person is offering ārati, is that, "Oh my beloved, more dear to me than my prāṇa, whatever obstacles may come—you have overcome so many obstacles to be here together—but in the future if any obstacles will come due to fate, then let all those problems, let all those obstacles, may all those difficulties fall on my head, but let you be free from all inconveniences. You should not suffer." So when the sakhīs are offering ārati to Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa, it is, they're offering their own lives. This is a gesture that, "You should be happy, you should not have any problem, you, no ill-fate should come to you. Whatever ill-fate was meant to come to you, it should come to me instead, but let you be happy." This is the meaning of (..) the mood of ārati in Vraja, whether Mother Yaśodā is offering or whether Lalitā and the sakhīs are offering to Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa. It's such an expression of love.

source.title: Specialities of Vrindavana Lila - 2023-01-15 - Sri Prem Prayojan

more.quote: I remember once my Gurudeva was on parikramā and he was meeting with one of his godbrothers. And this godbrother, he saw that Śrīla Gurudeva, he was having a pastime of some illness, but at the same time he was preaching and inspiring people all over the world. Whereas that godbrother, out of his humility, he was thinking, "I am not doing such service. I cannot inspire others, but I am quite healthy." So then when he was speaking, he said, "Oh, I am praying to Kṛṣṇa that whatever is left of my life and my health, oh, let it be taken away and give it to my godbrother, Śrīla Nārāyaṇa Mahārāja, so that he will be health and preach everywhere." Very sweet, (..)? So if the sādhakas in this world can have such a feeling for each other of love, then what to speak of the sakhīs in Vṛndāvana? Such selfless prema. So jaya jaya rādhā-kṛṣṇa yugala-milana, all the obstacles are over. Ārati karaye lalitādi-sakhī-gaṇa, and may there be no more obstacles. The sakhīs, "We will take everything on us, but let Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa be happy." Because their happiness is our happiness only. There's no separate interest.
